title: connector-mcp: a declarative `providerConfig.include` that is not an array is dropped and every tool is exposed, and an unknown tool name is ignored — refuse both at materialization, as `openapi` does (one meaning for `include`)
body:
epic:#27293#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcVBKAFk1ntXSjvPt7U

Filing gate: ① a product defect with a named location, `finding` class (c) (metadata an author writes that the runtime silently mis-honours), and the execution of an existing triage ruling. Found by the os-dev on #26709 (report comment 6488553467) and re-read by this seat. Child of #27293 (E1). ⛔ Not a claim.

`reach:` named producer — an author or AI writing `providerConfig.include` on a `provider: 'mcp'` declarative instance. Measured by the dev through `createMcpProviderFactory` (the factory the boot materializer calls) with a fake client listing `web_search` + `delete_everything`: `include: 'web_search'` (a string) → actions `[web_search, delete_everything]`, no error; `include: ['nope']` → `[]`, instance `ready`, no error; `include: ['web_search', 7]` → `[web_search]`.

## The defect

`packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts:223-226` (read at `origin/main`, 2026-10-29T05:10Z):

```ts
const includeList = Array.isArray(cfg.include)
  ? cfg.include.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string')
  : undefined;
const include = includeList ? (toolName: string) => includeList.includes(toolName) : undefined;
```

A non-array `include` becomes `undefined`, which means "no allowlist": the author asked to expose one tool and the instance exposes all of them. An unknown name is dropped silently, so a server that stops listing a tool surfaces as a flow failing at run time, not at boot.

## Governing text

Triage on #26709 (6487372008), verbatim: "⛔ `include` keeps one meaning across `openapi` and `mcp`: the same allowlist semantics as `mcp-provider.ts:48`, and not a second spelling." PR #27387 (#26709 item 1) makes the `openapi` `include` loud: a non-array or non-string shape and an unknown entry are fatal configuration faults at materialization. AGENTS.md Prime Directive #12 (refuse loudly, never a lenient consumer).

## Work

Refuse, in `createMcpProviderFactory`, (a) an `include` that is not an array of non-empty strings, before connecting, and (b) an entry naming a tool the server does not list, after `tools/list`, each as a plain configuration fault with the same message shape as the `openapi` provider's (PR #27387). `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, so the PR owes a contract review before landing. Tests: the three shapes above, plus the control (no `include` → every tool).

## Business reason

`include` is the allowlist an app author uses to keep destructive tools away from flows and agents. Today a one-character slip (a string instead of an array) exposes every tool the server has, with no error anywhere.

## Reader

The triage seat grades and routes it (the `domain:server` lane, `connector-mcp`); the epic PM of #27293 dispatches it after PR #27387 lands, so both providers share one message shape.

## Dedupe

The 500 most recent issues and PRs (all states, read 2026-10-29T04:10Z), titles grepped for `mcp.*include|include.*mcp|allowlist`: 0 hits; control `connector` on the same set: 10 hits.
